problem:
Arranged in **ascending order**, the solutions of the equation $2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{2}$ for ${0}^{∘}<x\le {360}^{∘},$ are $x=${{field-1}}${}^{∘}$ and $x=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\sqrt{2} & =\sqrt{2} \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})={135}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${135}^{∘}$ lies inside the specified domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={135}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the second quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/144ed33e7739fbaf17e3f81dd9ae2fd0a2d8e4d622ced7cb5dd60c8d177b6c01.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{45}^{∘} \\  & ={225}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions of the equation, arranged in ascending order, are $x={135}^{∘}$ and $x={225}^{∘}.$
